  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study evaluates the predictive potential of changes in microtissue barrier function to screen drugs associated with clinical diarrhea, reporting predictive accuracy metrics (84% and 83%) and sensitivity (50%) for MTT assay, and accuracy (77%) and sensitivity (57%) for Caco-2 TEER assay. It quantifies agreement between in vitro assay results and human clinical outcomes for a panel of drugs.",

  "arm_evidence": "The study assesses gastrointestinal toxicities (GITs) as adverse events (AE) and evaluates the predictive potential of microtissue barrier function to screen drugs associated with clinical diarrhea.",

    "oncology",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study mentions oncology drugs and discusses gastrointestinal toxicities (GITs) as common adverse events, which can be considered cross-cutting.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study uses human 3D gastrointestinal microtissues and Caco-2 cells, and also references preclinical animal studies (rodents and non-rodents) for comparison.",

    "rat",
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study references preclinical animal studies in rodents (rat) and non-rodents, and mentions primate studies for comparison of concordance rates.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study uses TEER (Transepithelial Electrical Resistance) as a measure of barrier function and also reports MTT viability assay results, correlating these with clinical diarrhea incidence."
